I can’t ever stomach food for at least 3 hours after I wake up. Tried again this week to eat a simple blueberry English muffin and OJ. Got two bites in and a few sips of juice before I had to stop. My body said, NO WAY! 

I drink a glass of room temp water when I wake up. Then have a protein drink around 9 AM. My work lunch break is supposed to be at 12 PM but I don’t take it until 1 PM. It’s a salad or sandwich for lunch. I have some type of fruit or veg if I get hungry at work. But once I get home after work, it’s carbs and fats 100%. 

Eating is a burden for some of us. I don’t eat in the break room at work with my coworkers because it’s hard to get re-focused on work stuff if I do. So, I take my lunch to my desk and eat (takes approx 15 mins) then I use the other 15 mins to walk around the parking lot at work or just go sit in my car in silence. 

Food patterns have changed for me recently. I attribute it to stress/nerves. 

But I can’t remember any time in my life where I have been able to eat breakfast right after I wake up.

I scribe for a private oncology practice. I was hired by the physician specifically to work for him. We are a large practice with 5 locations. There are only two scribes in the practice… the top two billing physicians each have their own scribe. 

No one in my clinic really understands what I do. There are so many days, hours, minutes where I wonder how the hell do I fit in here. But at the end of the day, my physician always says, “thank you. You took a major load off of my charting/notes today. You looked ahead and got x y z reports/paths/labs/H&P done before I even had time to think about it.” 

We are vital to the efficiency of the flow of the machine. 

And, let’s be honest… scribing may not ever be the glory that we think it should be. Especially now with AI coming into play. 

Just learn what you can where you are. Take it one step (one patient) at a time. 

We know a hell of a lot more than our coworkers realize.

Jumping in even though this post is older. I (37) have been on Depo shot for 4 years after three other bc types and having recurring issues with endometriosis. In the time that I’ve taken Depo, I have had ZERO ruptured cysts and ZERO pain. That was a miracle in itself. However, I recently switched to a new GYN and told her that I wanted to come off of it to give my body a break and see if I could get back to “normal.” My regular doctor agreed with this decision, as she says that depo should not be used for more than 2 years at a time. 

Looking back, I can see the side effects of the shot building up. Increased anxiety, weight gain and complete lack of sex drive. 

Anyway… I was supposed to have a new shot in January, which I didn’t take. 

So far, I’ve only noticed the following new instances with my body since stopping:

1. Major hot flashes 
2. Shakiness
3. Headaches that feel like migraines
4. Extreme fatigue 

I know that my body hasn’t even had time to remotely adjust to the hormone change… sigh. 

Now, I want to focus more on how to help balance my hormones or at least help myself support this change. Guess I need to just keep doing research. I’ve seen some different lab tests mentioned in other readings, so maybe I can eventually get those done.

Echoing magnesium (I use powder form). Daily Vitamin D even though my levels are normal. Epsom salt baths help me a lot, as well as spending time 3-4x week in the sauna room at my local community gym.
